head: kam-2
rule: กำ 'to close the hand' takes almost no compounds, and none of the 18 queued here. Its real compounds are already filed and they look alike: กำปั้น and กำมือ carry the etymology กำ + X outright, and กำหมัด is glossed with กำ itself. Everything left is a different word that merely begins with the syllable. Thai's กำ- initial vocabulary is dominated by the Khmer กំ- prefix and by แผลง alteration, and the etymologies say so one by one: กำจร ← ขจร, กำจัด ← ขจัด (Khmer កំចាត់), กำราบ ← กราบ (Khmer កំរាប), กำเดา ← เขดา (Khmer ក្ដៅ), กำไร ← ไกร. Others are outright borrowings (กำปั่น from Malay kapal, กำยาน from kemenyan, ระกำ from Malay), one is a single inherited etymon (กำพร้า < Proto-Tai *ɡm̩.raːꟲ), one is a respelling of another word (กำโชก = กรรโชก), and one is a place name (กำปัง, tambon in Non Thai district). The rule for this head is therefore a NEGATIVE one: a กำ- word belongs to this head only where a source writes กำ + X or the gloss names the hand. Nothing else does.
